Once you know how to use a resistance band, there are lots of different workouts you can do! One of the easiest is a strength-training workout. Just imagine you’re lifting weights, but lighter and you can do all the movements with a resistance band instead of using weights. Here’s a summary of different exercises:

Bands for full body strength training: push-ups, deadlifts, squats, lunges, squats with band in front, push-ups with band around back, rows, chest press, pull-ups, dips, goblet squats, leg press, bent-over rows, lateral raises, tricep extensions.
Bands for upper body strength training: chin-ups, rope climbs, bent-over rows, deadlifts (also great for upper body strength), military presses, overhead press, bicep curls, tricep extensions, push-ups.

I could go on for hours, so you can click through to find out all the detail. Here’s an example of a full body strength-training workout that you can try out using a resistance band:

Start in the middle of an indoor track or basketball court. As a warm-up, run or walk around or jump rope.

Do 10–30 reps of each of the exercises below. You should feel these exercises in your shoulders, back, quads, chest, biceps, shoulders, triceps, and legs. A lot of bands have a 30-day challenge attached to them, but I’ll just give you a very quick summary of what you should expect for each.

Push-ups. 20–40 reps. You can do this anywhere, using a wall or another body part as support for your back in a push-up. I recommend using a bench, wall, or another body part that has space underneath you to catch your body when you are in the push-up position.

Deadlifts. 10–20 reps. You are lying on one flat surface (ground) with a band around the legs. The band is attached to the band pegs in the middle of the legs that are slightly above the knees. You can use the feet to push against the floor. Try to lift your legs straight above your head. The band makes this more challenging than it would be as it is not as free to move.

Squats. 10–20 reps. The same principles apply to squats in the body part where you place the band with your feet. The band makes this more challenging than it would be as it is not as free to move.

Chin-ups. 10–20 reps. Two basic pieces of advice here! Firstly it can feel very strange to start with and that is ok, take a deep breath and just get the body moving and going. Secondly, try to hold the position for as long as you can, maybe even as long as you can do a full push-up, the longer you hold the body becomes more stable. It will feel like a lot of strain, but it will help you get stronger and feel good when you give it a try again.

Lunges. 10–20 reps. Lie on a mat or towel on the floor with the band around your legs, the bottom of your feet should be pointing towards the ceiling. You can also bend over and lie on the ground with the band around your legs and the top of your body (your thighs aligned). Try to keep your hips level, use a wall or another person for support if you need to as you are in the down position. 

Bicep curls. 10–20 reps. Hold this position in a half push-up position, this will feel good to have something to focus your arms on, but this time the band is not the supporting factor. Take a few deep breaths in and out, relax the shoulders and relax for half a second and then jerk the band towards the knees as hard as you can.

Take a few deep breaths in and out, relax the shoulders and relax for half a second and then jerk the band towards the knees as hard as you can.

Goblet squats. Hold this position in a squat position and squat down until the bar is low on the ground, this will take great strength and endurance. This exercise requires you to use the muscles in the legs that control your balance, rather than just the muscles in the back.

Leg press. Hold this position in a squat and extend the legs as far away from the body as possible, lift the legs together and lower back down slowly, this requires great strength and balance to get it right.
